description: Hi everyone! I’m Jeevan, a 1st-year Computer Engineering student at the University of Waterloo. I’m passionate about building end-to-end engineering solutions that bridge hardware, low-level software, and intelligent data systems. Whether it's developing real-time embedded systems, tinkering with sensor networks, or deploying high-performance desktop/web applications, I love taking ideas from concept to functional prototype.
summary:
Are wildfires becoming more severe, or are our satellites simply becoming better at detecting them? Our team developed EPOCH (Earth’s Planetary Observation and Critical Hotspot Engine) to address this challenge and make decades of NASA Earth observation data more meaningful.

EPOCH is an interactive wildfire exploration platform that transforms satellite observations into a historical activity calendar. Users can explore regions of interest on a 3D globe, compare wildfire seasons, identify recurring peak burning periods, and recognize unusually active years. The platform also includes a machine-learning research viewer for investigating differences between satellite detections and a wildfire response simulator for exploring potential firefighting strategies.

Our project addresses the NASA Space Apps Challenge by connecting historical fire patterns with practical questions about seasonal preparedness. Understanding when and where wildfire activity typically intensifies can help fire managers prioritize monitoring and better understand emerging risks. EPOCH aims to make complex satellite observations accessible, scientifically comparable, and useful for environmental awareness and wildfire preparedness.
details:
Was 2023 an exceptional wildfire summer, or were newer satellites simply seeing more? EPOCH turns this question into an interactive data story, combining geospatial intelligence and Earth observation to support wildfire preparedness.

Our 3D globe and weekly calendar let users compare June–August activity (2003–2026) across 50–70°N, 140–60°W, uncover anomalies, identify peak monitoring periods and export CSV data.

Using NASA FIRMS MODIS and VIIRS detections, our Python pipeline creates daily 0.25° cells, weights for latitude, masks persistent heat sources and estimates archive gaps. A power-law conversion harmonizes VIIRS with MODIS, achieving 5.4% median absolute percentage error versus 9.3% for a fixed ratio in leave-one-season-out validation. On this scale, 2023 ranked first of 24 summers at four times the median of the others.

Our PLSWORK MLP learns from 96 MODIS features and VIIRS labels. In a regional benchmark, unmatched alerts fell from 93 to 72, while matched positives fell from 76 to 70. A research viewer visualizes cached predictions across 84 patches and exports GeoJSON. A simulator uses terrain, weather and detections to explore aircraft and crew tactics in Jasper, Yellowknife and Hay River.

Built with JavaScript, React, Three.js, Vite, Python, PyTorch and FastAPI, EPOCH bridges satellite data and evidence-informed decision support while considering sensor bias, uncertainty and detection trade-offs. Hotspots are not burned area; simulations are illustrative.
